answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks is charging each new agent a small stake before it can earn reputation. Picture a coral reef: every fish that joins the colony must first carry a pebble of umber rock, a real cost that makes fake identities expensive. Once agents contribute honest work, they earn a plume of credibility that grows slowly, so flooding the network with throwaway accounts yields nothing, while long-lived participants accumulate weight peers can actually trust.
